"Dharma Guru" Gyan Swarup Ji Maharaj (October 21, 1895-February 25, 1985) was a leading saint of the Sanatani Dharma tradition within the Regar community.
Initiation
Initiated from the Jishi Math of Jagat Guru Shankaracharya, resident of Tirtharaj Pushkar, supreme disciple of Paramhans Swami Brahmanand Ji Maharaj, Swami Maujiram Ji Maharaj ('Mauj Ashram' Mirpur Sakh Sindh which is currently in Pakistan), after being initiated and cultured in the Advaita philosophy of religion and sixteen rituals, "Swami Gyanswaroopananda" was dedicated for the welfare of mankind.
Social and religious titles
* "Raigar Ratna" On September 27, 1986, the "Fifth All India Regar Mahasammelan" was held at "Vigyan Bhawan" in New Delhi, under the chairmanship of Shri Dharamdas Shastri (former Member of Parliament), the then President of the All India Regar Mahasabha (Regd.), and in the special presence of His Excellency Shri Giani Zail Singh, the then President of India. In recognition of Swami Gyan Swarup Maharaj's outstanding services to society, His Excellency honored him, after his death, by awarding him a gold medal and the title of "Raigar Ratna" from the Government of India. This title was accepted by Swami Ji's successor disciple, Swami Shri Ramanand 'Jigyasu' Ji.
*"Title of Dharma Guru": On September 18, 1988, at the "Sanatan Dharma Pratinidhi Sammelan" organized by the All India Sanatan Dharma Pratinidhi Sabha at the Talkatora Indoor Stadium in New Delhi under the chairmanship of Dr. Girdhari Lal Goswami, the then Vice President of India, His Excellency Dr. Shankar Dayal Sharma, in the presence of Jagat Guru Shankaracharya Shri Shri Bharati Tirtha Maharaj of the Sringeri Math, honored Swami Gyanswarup Maharaj with the title of "Dharma Guru" for his distinguished service to Sanatan Dharma after his nirvana and for his dedicated services to the welfare of the people with goodwill. The title was accepted by Shri Hemendra Kumar Mohanpuria (former Municipal Councillor), the then President of Swami Maujiram Satsang Sabha.
At this same representative conference, other saints, including Saint Baba Nagpal Ji Maharaj of Shri Adyakatyayani Shaktipeeth, Chhattarpur Temple, Delhi, Saint Ramchandra Dogre Maharaj of Maharashtra, and Saint Murari Bapu Ji of Gujarat, were also honored with the title of "Dharma Guru."
The above-mentioned decorations and titles received by Swami Gyanswarup Ji Maharaj are a result of his social and religious welfare efforts.
Early life
Swamiji was born  on October 21, 1895, Ashwin Shukla Triyodashi Vikram Samvat 1952 in village Gohana, district Ajmer (Rajasthan) as the son of Shrimati Mendi Bai, the wife of Shri Udaram Gusainwal of Raigar community. Swamiji's birth name was Genaram.
Genaram's parents were religious, which led to his receiving religious upbringing from an early age. Genaram was sent to school for his childhood. His father wanted his son to learn to read and recite religious texts like the Gita, Ramayana, Mahabharata, and other scriptures.
Genaram gained considerable proficiency in Hindi from his primary education. However, due to the declining population of Gohana village, the school was relocated to Rajkiyawas village. Despite his dedication to studies, he was unable to pursue further education. In his teenage years, Swamiji's study of religious and spiritual books, coupled with his family environment, led to his developing a devotion to God. He then began a life of contemplation. Once, Swami Moujiram Ji visited Gohana village. He was quite famous. On such an occasion, young Genaram listened to and internalized his instructive discourse. Swami Maujiram Ji said, "Everyone should always remain steadfast in good thoughts." He elaborated on the religious teachings that pave the way from materialism to spirituality, deeply influencing young Genaram. From then on, he became aloof from family life. His father died in 1910, and his mother, sister-in-law, a brother, and a nephew died in 1914. After some time, the elders of the family began efforts to arrange Genaram's marriage. However, he resolved to renounce all worldly attachments, offer himself at the feet of Swami Maujiram Ji, and devote himself to renunciation.
Religious life
Guru's refuge
Having renounced all worldly attachments, Genaram Ji arrived at "Mauj Ashram" in Mirpur Khas, Sindh (Pakistan). He remained in the company of Swami Maujiram Ji for approximately two years in 1915-16. Subsequently, on August 12, 1917, at the age of 21, on the occasion of Rakshabandhan, Swami Maujiram Ji, pleased with Genaram's devotion and service to the Guru, granted him discipleship as "Gyanswaroopanand." After initiation, Gyanswaroop Ji stayed at the Guru's Ashram for several years, learning from the Guru in the fields of Gyan Yoga, Karma Yoga, and Bhakti Yoga. He also engaged in in-depth self-study of the scriptures.
Traveling India and social upliftment
After attaining enlightenment, he traveled India and saw that society was in a very dire state spiritually, socially, and economically. He resolved to transform society and engaged in social upliftment. He worked towards social upliftment by raising public awareness through satsangs, conferences, and rallies to end social evils.
Scripture composition
Along with his work for social renewal, Swamiji also worked to raise spiritual awareness by composing religious texts and scriptures. The scriptures he authored are:
* Gyan Bhajan Prabhakar
* Atha Atmagyan Bhaskar
* Sandhyaadi Nityakarma
* Kundaliyan
Conferences
To improve the condition of society, Swami Gyanswarup Ji made a special contribution by inspiring the All-India Regar Samaj Mahasammelan, in which his disciple, Swami Atmaram 'Lakshya' Ji, played a special role. Other communities also drew inspiration from his work.
*Historic Mahasammelan  On May 28-29, 1944, a workers' conference was held under the chairmanship of Swami Gyanswaroop Ji Maharaj, and it was decided to hold the first Mahasammelan in Dausa on November 2, 3, and 4, 1944. In the presence of Swami Gyanswarup Ji, Swami Ji's closest disciple, Swami Atmaram Ji 'Lakshya', founded the All India Regar Mahasabha. At this Mahasammelan, Shri Bholaram Taungaria Ji was appointed President of the All India Regar Mahasabha.
*Second Mahasammelan:  Held in Jaipur on April 12-13, 1946, a grand procession and rally was held, including Swamiji's Victoria Chariot. Swami Atmaram "Lakshya" inaugurated the conference by hoisting the flag. Maharaj Gyan Swarup Ji, as a visionary guide, presented his views to society, highlighting the importance of education and saying:
Both of the above conferences were organized by Swami Gyanswarup Ji Maharaj and Swami Atmaram Ji 'Lakshya'. The work of the devotees, social workers, and the Delhi Provincial Volunteer Board was also commendable. At this conference, Shri Kanhaiyalal Ratawal Ji was appointed President of the All India Regar Mahasabha.
*Third Mahasammelan:  The Third Pushkar Mahasammelan, held on November 17, 18, and 19, 1964, was inaugurated by Swami Gyanswarup Ji Maharaj. The program was presided over by Shri Naval 'Prabhakar' Jajoria, a resident of Delhi and the then Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha) from Karol Bagh. Resolutions passed at previous Mahasammelans were considered, and socially beneficial proposals were adopted. Shri Naval 'Prabhakar' Ji was appointed President of the All India Regar Mahasabha.
*Ajmer All India Regar Mahasabha Executive Meeting:  In the meeting of All India Regar Mahasabha Executive and eminent persons held in Ajmer on 8-9 October, 1977, under resolution number 6, Shri Chhogalal Kanwaria ji was made the President of All India Regar Mahasabha.
*Fourth Mahasammelan:  Held in Jaipur on October 6-7, 1984, with the blessings of Swami Gyan Swarup and the efforts of Shri Dharamdas Shastri, then Member of Parliament from Karol Bagh, the conference was attended by the then Prime Minister of India and world leader, Mrs. Indira Gandhi, as a special guest, honoring the Regar community. At this time, the President of the All India Regar Mahasabha was Shri Chhogalal Kanwaria, former Health Minister of the Rajasthan Government. Shri Dharamdas Shastri, Member of Parliament, was declared the newly appointed President at this conference. Swami Ramanand 'Jigyasu' was also present.
*31st Annual Mahotsav: of the then Sanatan Dharma Satsang Sabha (present Swami Maujiram Satsang Sabha) was celebrated with great enthusiasm on 9-10 April 1949 at Vishnu Mandir, 18, Raigarpura under the chairmanship of Goswami Shri Ganesh Dutt Maharaj Ji, disciple of Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya Ji and in the presence of Swami Gyanswaroop Ji Maharaj. Among the eminent religious people present at the festival were Seth 'Sir' of Delhi Cloth Mills, Shri Jugal Kishore Birla of the Shri Ram-Birla family, Lok Sabha Deputy Speaker Shri Anant Shaynam Iyengar, Dr. Khub Ram Jajoria, member of the then Chief Commissioner's Advisory Committee, Delhi and Goswami Girdhari Lal Shastri, etc. The then-President of the Satsang Sabha, Shri Ramswaroop Jajoria and Minister Shri Kanwar Sain Maurya played a very special and noteworthy role.
Construction of hostels for the promotion of education
In 1950, Swami Gyanswarup Ji Maharaj established the Shri Gyan Ganga Hostel at Nagori Gate (Jodhpur, Rajasthan) in the Marwar region. Currently, the Shri Gyan Ganga Hostel is run by the Rajasthan Jatiya (Regar) Vikas Sabha (Regd.). Swami Gyan Swarup Maharaj was its first president. Following this tradition, a hostel was also established in Khetnadi, Mandore Road, Jodhpur (Rajasthan), where Swami Gopal Ram Ji and Swami Ramanand 'Jigyasu' Ji have performed significant work. The "Tyagmurti Swami Atmaram 'Lakshya' Hostel" was also established in Ringas (Rajasthan), a result of Swami Gyan Swarup Ji's inspiration. The Regar Hostel currently under construction in Jaipur will be a continuation of this tradition.
After the partition of India on August 15, 1947, Swamiji returned from Sindh to Beawar. After staying with Amar Patel for a period, he built an ashram in Bada Bas. In 1953, Swamiji moved from Bada Bas to the newly allotted "Gyanswarup Advaita Ashram" in Jatiya Colony, Nehru Nagar, Beawar, Rajasthan. Swamiji spent the rest of his life there. It is now known as the "Dharam Guru Gyanswarup Advaita Ashram." The ashram's wooden slippers, kamandal, Rudraksha beads, handwritten manuscripts, and rare texts still evoke the presence of the great saint, Swami Swarup, and are preserved in memory.
Establishment of religious places
* Vishnu Temple (Karol Bagh): The Vishnu Temple was built at 18, Raigarpura, Karol Bagh, in the heart of Delhi, the capital of India, through the generous efforts of Swami Moujiram Ji Maharaj and Swami Gyanswaroop Ji and their disciples living in Delhi. Maharaj Ji used to stay and rest at this place whenever he came to Delhi. For this reason, before the construction of the temple, this place was famous as "Gurudwara". This is the Gangdhara of the all-welfare religion and the "Gyanswaroop tradition" started in the society by Swami Moujiram Ji Maharaj. Swami Atmaram Ji 'Lakshya'; The Vishnu Temple in Raigarpura Karol Bagh, Delhi is the most important resting place and memorial place in the name of Swami Ramanand Ji 'Jigyasu' and Swami Anantananda Ji (Pt. Chunnilal Saukariya) and revered saints. On the second floor of the temple, "Dharamguru Swami Gyanswaroop Satsang Sabhagar" is built, in which, along with the statues of senior gurus, a magnificent and radiant statue of Swami Gyanswaroop Ji is installed in the middle of the Sabhagar.
* Shaligram Temple (Malusar): On 25 May 1951, the idol was installed and the temple Kalash flag was hoisted by Swami Gyan Swaroop Ji in the Shaligram Temple located in Malusar, Ajmer (Rajasthan) and a program of social reform was started in this area through a Panchayat.
* Ganga Mai Temple (Santnagar, New Delhi):  In 1957, the idol of Shri Ganga Mai Ji was consecrated by Swami Ji in Santnagar Karol Bagh.
* Shri Triveni Ganga Temple (Saiwad):  The idol of Shri Ganga Mata was consecrated in this temple by Swamiji on March 5, 1969 in village Saiwad (Rajasthan).
* Shri Ganga Temple (Beawar):  The foundation stone of Shri Ganga Mai Temple was laid by Swamiji on 20-04-1976 in Jatiya Colony Beawar.
* Shri Baba Ramdev Temple (Beedanpura New Delhi Karol Bagh):  The idol of Shri Baba Ramdev Ji was consecrated by Swami Ji on 18th September, 1980.
* Jigyasu Ashram (Pipar): In 1982, Swami Gyanswarup Ji Maharaj laid the foundation stone for a massive ashram in Pipar town (Rajasthan). Swami Ramanand Jigyasu Ji completed the work. This ashram is known as "Jigyasu Ashram" for its grandeur and vastness.
* Raigar Dharamshala, Haridwar:  The Raigar Dharamshala, located on Birla Road in Haridwar was inaugurated on June 19, 1983, in your presence, thanks to the tireless efforts of Swami Ramanand Jigyasu (Pipar) and Swami Gopal Ram Ji Maharaj (Nagaur).
Jagriti Patra Prakashan Samiti
The "Jagriti Patra Prakashan Samiti" was established on October 2, 1948, under the chairmanship of Swami Gyan Swarupji, and the first issue of the national newspaper "Jagriti" was published on the same day. The editorship was assumed by freedom fighter Shri Suryamal Maurya, a resident of Beawar. Only 30 issues of this newspaper were published.
Death and funeral
Swami Ramanand Ji died on February 25, 1985, in the presence of Jigyasu-Ashram, Pipar city, Jodhpur (Rajasthan). As soon as the news of Swami Ji's death was received, his devoted disciples from across the country came to Jigyasu Ashram to pay their last respects. Swami Ji's body was kept for the darshan of devotees from February 26-27, 1985. On February 28, 1985, a grand funeral procession was taken out in the presence of thousands of his devotees. His body was consigned to flames with Vedic mantras.
Major institutions of Delhi Province under the system of Dharmaguru Gyanswaroopji Maharaj
* Guru Gyanswaroop Sumiran Samiti (Regd.), Karol Bagh, New Delhi
* Swami Maujiram Satsang Sabha (Regd.), Raigarpura
* 'Dharmaguru' Swami Gyanswaroop Satsang Sabha (Regd.), Madipur
